title: Signal Heist
summary: Crack a vault lock by rebuilding its signal from pure tones with trigonometric identities, then charge the fuse with the integral.
subject: mathematics
concepts: sin² x and cos² x by the double angle formula
Products to sums: 2 sin A cos B and the like
Powers such as sin³ x and cos⁴ x
Triple products of sines and cosines
Integrating a sum of pure tones
Net value of a definite integral that changes sign
learningOutcome: The student can rewrite powers and products of sines and cosines as sums with trigonometric identities, integrate the result, and evaluate the definite integral.

levels.title: Double angle locks
levels.adds: Baseline: sin² x = (1 − cos 2x)/2 and cos² x = (1 + cos 2x)/2 turn a square into pure tones you can integrate (Ex 7.3 Q1; Example 7).
hints: Use cos 2x = 1 − 2 sin² x = 2 cos² x − 1.
A constant is a tone of frequency 0: the first slot.

levels.title: Product locks
levels.adds: New: products to sums, 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A − B), and the cos cos and sin sin forms (Ex 7.3 Q2, Q7).
hints: 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A − B); 2 cos A cos B = cos(A + B) + cos(A − B).
2 sin A sin B = cos(A − B) − cos(A + B).
If A < B, sin(A − B) is negative: sin(−2x) = −sin 2x.

levels.title: Power and triple locks
levels.adds: Harder: cubes and fourth powers, and products of three, need the identities twice (Ex 7.3 Q3, Q4, Q6, Q10, Q11).
hints: sin 3x = 3 sin x − 4 sin³ x and cos 3x = 4 cos³ x − 3 cos x.
cos⁴ x = (cos² x)²: use the double angle formula twice.
For three factors, turn two of them into a sum first, then multiply by the third.

levels.title: Charge the fuse
levels.adds: New: evaluate the definite integral from 0 to π/2 after the identity; parts below the axis count as negative (Ex 7.3 with Ex 7.8).
hints: Rewrite the product as a sum of pure tones first.
Integrate each tone: ∫ sin kx dx = −(cos kx)/k and ∫ cos kx dx = (sin kx)/k.
Put in π/2 and 0 and subtract; the lock reads the net charge.

misconceptions: A definite integral of a wave is always positive
